metadata.title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Backport vllm-project/vllm#57477, #58454: seed the kpool tail through its padded stride, size the tail ring for speculative drafts
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Backports of two upstream fixes for the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer tail cache, in the same form as the earlier backports (#657, #1406). main does not have them. Both change only the NVIDIA kpool code that 1Cat runs for GLM-5.3-Flash on V100 (SparseAttnIndexerKpool admits CUDA without DeepGEMM only on exact SM70), and both corrupt pool keys that the indexer ranks once a request's context is longer than index_topk (2048 tokens).

vllm-project/vllm#57477 ([Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel, upstream commit db1bfdd4f, by Jared Wen). The prefill seed kernel _kpool_tail_seed_kernel in vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py addressed the tail cache as a dense [num_blocks, 2, kpool, head_dim] array (base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM). On main the tail tensor is a strided view onto its sibling indexer tensor: _get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next in vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py pads the KpoolTailSpec page to the indexer page (38016 B at 1152-token blocks, 288 pool rows of 132 B, against 2048 B for a dense fp16 or bf16 tail block), and the decode kernel in the same file already addresses the tail through stride(0) and stride(1). So every prefill wrote its last kpool raw K and gate rows into the indexer blocks at the start of the layer's indexer region and left the request's own tail block unseeded. The first pool that decode completes after a prompt whose length is not a multiple of kpool was then compressed from whatever the tail block's previous owner left there, and the overwritten indexer rows belong to the blocks handed out first, typically a prefix-cached system prompt, which keeps the damage. The fix passes tail.stride(0) and tail.stride(1) to the seed kernel and asserts the view layout. Adaptations: main's kpool_seed_tail_cache also accepts fp16 (the tail takes the model dtype, fp16 on V100), upstream's is bf16-only; that dtype assert is kept and upstream's two layout asserts are added next to it. Upstream's test hunk renames an AMD-only test that this file never had, so test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride is added as a new test, parametrized over bf16 and fp16.

vllm-project/vllm#58454 ([Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] kpool corruption with speculative decoding, upstream commit 2617fe938, by Matt Mastracci). The tail ring had exactly index_kpool (4) slots (Glm5NextTailCache.get_kv_cache_spec in vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py), and _kpool_decode_update_batched_kernel addressed it by pos % kpool. A verify step stashes every draft into the ring before acceptance is known. When a pool-completing draft is rejected, the drafts stashed behind it have already overwritten that pool's committed keys, and the redo of the pool in the next step compresses wrong keys. Per upstream this affects any speculative method with num_speculative_tokens >= 2 and only pools built during decode; the DFlash2 routes documented for GLM-5.3 on V100 (docs/design/sm70_glm53_flash_nvfp4.md) use q7, i.e. 8 tokens per verify step into a 4-slot ring. The ring now holds kpool * next_power_of_2(cdiv(kpool + num_speculative_tokens, kpool)) slots (4 without speculation as before, 8 with one draft token, 16 with seven), both kernels address it by pos % RING with RING = tail.shape[2], and the pool phase stays pos % kpool. get_kv_cache_spec asserts that the ring divides cache_config.block_size, as upstream does. The fp16 tail page grows from 2 KiB to 8 KiB at 16 slots and stays padded to the indexer page it shares (38016 B at 1152-token blocks; a page that did not fit would trip the existing page_size_padded assert in vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py), so the KV cache memory is unchanged. The scheduler block (lcm of the group block sizes) stays the attention block because the ring divides it; where the hash block size is the gcd of the group block sizes (resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes), it becomes the ring instead of 4. Adaptations: upstream changes vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py and the AMD kernels, which main does not have; the spec change goes into main's NVIDIA Glm5NextTailCache with main's spec form (num_kv_heads=1, head_size=2*head_dim, model dtype), and the decode wrapper keeps its fp16 dtype assert. compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping in vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py names its parameter ring (its caller already passes the spec's block_size), and comments that said ring == kpool are updated (indexer.py, sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py, kv_cache_utils.py). Upstream's tail-ring spec test imports the GLM model package at module level; here the import sits inside the test, so the file's other tests do not depend on it, and since that import works on main without a GPU, the test runs on CPU. test_glm53_pp2_kpool_tail_shares_indexer_storage in tests/v1/core/test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py also runs with a 16-slot ring (page fit and shared indexer storage).

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs and issues of this repository for 57477, 58454, kpool, "kpool tail", "tail ring", "padded indexer stride", "kpool speculative", "GLM-5.3 speculative" and "seed kernel"; none backports either fix. The open #1260 (serving GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF across seven GPUs, 215 files, in conflict with main) contains equivalent changes to the same code as part of that feature, without naming them in its description: its NVIDIA seed kernel addresses the tail through stride(0) and stride(1), and its tail holds kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_speculative_tokens, kpool) slots (12 with seven draft tokens). This PR carries only the two upstream fixes with their tests, in upstream's merged form (a power-of-two number of pools, and the assert that the ring divides the attention block); whichever lands second drops the duplicated parts. Other open PRs that touch the same files: #1286 and #1348 (both mine) change other parts of kpool_compress.py and attention.py, #1347 and #1282 (mine) and #828 other parts of sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py; this branch merges cleanly with each of them (git merge-tree). The open issue #1330 (KVBlockZeroer on the virtually split indexer cache) is a different defect. Upstream, #57534 (a Triton fusion of the tail slot mapping, a performance change) and #58704 (SM90 FlashInfer sparse MLA) refer to these PRs and do not apply here.

AI assistance was used for this backport. I reviewed every line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/core/test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/core/test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py on a Tesla V100 and on a Quadro RTX 8000, on this branch and on main c98a8d664 (same build of the native libraries)
python -m pytest <this branch's tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py> -k "padded_tail_block_stride or rejected_draft_redo or decode_writer_matches_prefill" from a main c98a8d664 checkout on a Tesla V100, i.e. the new cases against main's kernels
TRITON_INTERPRET=1 with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="": tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py on CPU tensors (device strings set to cpu), once with this branch's kpool_compress.py and once with main's and with the first commit's in its place (the GLM package __init__ replaced by an empty package so the kernel module can be swapped).
test_tail_ring_divides_the_attention_block on CPU, once with main's vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py in place of this branch's.
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| kpool prefill tail seed (kpool_seed_tail_cache, _kpool_tail_seed_kernel) | tail in the model dtype (fp16 on SM70); bf16 and fp16 in the tests | tail tensor is a strided view onto the indexer tensor, page padded to the indexer page; every prefill or prefill chunk | each request's last pool rows land in its own tail block, addressed by stride(0)/stride(1); no route change | executed on a Tesla V100: the new seed test fails with main's kernel (bf16 and fp16) and passes here; the same under TRITON_INTERPRET=1 | GLM-5.3-Flash end to end on this branch |
| kpool decode and spec-verify stash and pool completion (kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_batched) | same | ring = kpool * next_power_of_2(cdiv(kpool + num_speculative_tokens, kpool)): 4 without speculation (unchanged), 8 with one draft token, 16 with q7 DFlash2 | the redo of a rejected pool-completing draft reads the committed keys | executed on a Tesla V100: the ring_pools=2 cases fail with main's kernel and pass here; the same under TRITON_INTERPRET=1 | DFlash2 and MTP end to end on this branch |
| tail KV spec and cache layout (Glm5NextTailCache.get_kv_cache_spec, _get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next) | KpoolTailSpec, page padded to the indexer page | ring must divide cache_config.block_size (asserted); the ring page must fit the indexer page (existing page_size_padded assert) | KV cache memory and scheduler block unchanged; gcd hash block = ring | executed: test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py (ring 4 and 16), spec test on CPU | PD / KV-connector transfer of the larger tail page |
| tail slot mapping (compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping) | int32 slots | slot = own_block * ring + pos % ring, ring = spec block_size | identical to before for ring 4 | executed: test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py | none |
| SM75 | n/a | main admits the GLM-5.3 kpool indexer on CUDA without DeepGEMM only on exact SM70 | not reachable on main | source | Turing admission is part of #1286 |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: always on; bug fix, not a performance change.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: n/a (no benchmark; not a performance change).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: this branch on main c98a8d664; the same two patches run on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, fork-main-v6 0b342e7b5).
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: none.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: not a performance change. On our fork, the bundle of 31 upstream backports that contains these two passed an A/B against the same tree without the bundle (logs ab_v6f_glm_2026-11-07a.log and ab_v6f_dsv4_2026-11-07a.log). GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 with DFlash2, PP5 over three V100 and two RTX 8000 (arms T T P T P): prefill of 8687 tokens 3.86 s in every arm, short decode 40.38 to 40.41 tok/s (T) against 40.45 to 40.47 tok/s (P), GSM8K-30 29 correct in every arm, eight quality texts token-identical, first token at 516196 prompt tokens 197.21 s against 197.46 s. DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP5 (arms T P T P): prefill of 8921 tokens 2.28 s, short decode 55.88 against 55.87 tok/s, GSM8K-30 29 correct in every arm, eight quality texts token-identical, first token at 486316 prompt tokens 145.88 s against 145.90 s. These runs show no regression; they are not a reproducer of the two defects.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed; the ring follows num_speculative_tokens.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

On this branch (main c98a8d664 + these two commits):
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="": tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py 17 passed; tests/v1/core/test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py 5 passed.
- test_tail_ring_divides_the_attention_block with main's attention.py: 4 failed, 1 passed (ring 4 for every draft count); with this branch: 5 passed (rings 4/8/8/16/32 for 0/1/4/7/13 draft tokens).
- tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py under TRITON_INTERPRET=1 on CPU, the eight new or changed cases (test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride, test_rejected_draft_redo_needs_ring_slots, test_decode_writer_matches_prefill_writer): this branch 8 passed; main's kernel file 5 failed, 3 passed (both seed cases, the request's own tail block keeps the sentinel; the three ring_pools=2 cases, main's wrapper asserts ring == kpool); the first commit's kernel file 3 failed, 5 passed (the ring_pools=2 cases). test_rejected_draft_redo_needs_ring_slots[1] passes with every kernel: it asserts that a one-pool ring corrupts the redone pool.
- The whole file under the interpreter: this branch 24 passed, 10 failed; main's kernel file 19 passed, 15 failed. The 10 are the same reference-based cases with both kernels (test_batched_matches_reference, its fuzz variant and test_leading_invalid_tail_slot), so the interpreter run does not replace the GPU run.
- pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: every hook passes except check-layering, which reports vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py (platform coupling 25 -> 32) and vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (37 -> 39); this PR touches neither file, the report is the same on main c98a8d664.
- pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: passed.
- Tesla V100: tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py 34 passed (main: 28 passed, the file's cases before this PR); tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py 17 passed (main: 10 passed); tests/v1/core/test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py 5 passed (main: 4 passed).
- Tesla V100, this branch's kernel test file run against main's kernels (-k "padded_tail_block_stride or rejected_draft_redo or decode_writer_matches_prefill"): 5 failed, 3 passed, the same five cases as under the interpreter.
- Quadro RTX 8000: test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py 17 passed and test_glm5_kv_cache_layout.py 5 passed (main: 10 and 4). test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py: 32 failed, 2 passed (the two seed cases); on main 28 failed. Every failure is the same Triton compile error of _kpool_decode_update_batched_kernel or _kpool_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel ("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture"), on main as on this branch: main runs the kpool indexer only on exact SM70 (see the SM75 row above).

On our fork (the same two patches, fork-main-v6 0b342e7b5, which also carries our Turing support from #1286): tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py 34 passed and tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py 17 passed, on a Tesla V100 and on a Quadro RTX 8000.
